summary: Ding-hwa Evelyn Hsieh works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. She completed her PhD at the University of California, Los Angeles, and was appointed professor of Philosophy and Religion at Truman State University in 1998.

Dipa Ma (1911–1989) was a Buddhist and religious studies figure. She studied under Mahasi Sayadaw (~1967–1968) and Anagarika Munindra (~1967–1969), and taught Sharon Salzberg, Joseph Goldstein, Jack Kornfield, and Sylvia Boorstein.

Dipak Kumar Barua is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. At the University of Calcutta, he was an Assistant Lecturer in Pali (attested 1979) and Dean (1987). He later served as head (学長) of Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (~1996–2003).

Dipak Ranjan Das specializes in Indology, history, and archaeology. A student of Dineschandra Sircar, he served as a Lecturer at Sanskrit College and University (attested 1966) and in the Department of Ancient Indian History and Culture at the University of Calcutta (attested 1994).

Dipankar Bhattacharya works in Indology and linguistics. He pursued his PhD at National Sanskrit University (2023–2026) and served as Project Manager for Content and Research at Rishihood University in 2025.

Dipesh Chakrabarty is a historian and philosopher who earned a PhD from the Australian National University (~1977–1980). After teaching at the University of Melbourne (~1984–1995), he was appointed Lawrence A. Kimpton Distinguished Service Professor at the University of Chicago in 1995.

Dirk H. A. Kolff is an Indologist and historian who earned his MA (~1960–1967) and doctorate (~1978–1983) from Leiden University. He served at Leiden as a lecturer (1967) and held the Chair of Indian History (1971–2003).
Dirk Huizinga (1840–1903) studied at the University of Groningen (~1858–1867) and later held a post there from 1870 to 1901.

Dirk Jan Hoens (1920–2003) was a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He studied at Utrecht University under Jan Gonda, earning a PhD (1939–1951) and Dr.Theol. (~1945–1955), and served as an Assistant at Utrecht University (1948–1982).
Dirk Schmidt is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied for a PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (attested 2026), where he was a PhD student and teaching assistant in 2022.

Dirk van Hinloopen Labberton (1874–1961), a scholar of Indology and linguistics, earned PhDs from Leiden (-1927) and Amsterdam (-1929). He taught at Gymnasium Willem III, Bestuursschool, and the University of Tokyo, and was teacher and Rector at Theosofisch Lyceum (~1930–1937).

Divya Prakash Pathak specializes in computational linguistics and Indology. He completed an MA in Sanskrit at Jawaharlal Nehru University (2021–2023) and became a Research Scholar at the University of Delhi in 2023.

Divyaraj Amiya is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. As attested in 2026, he held positions as a faculty member at the University of Tübingen and as a Temporary Teaching Fellow in Hindi at the University of Zurich.

Diwakar Acharya, an Indology, religious studies, and philosophy scholar, earned a PhD at the University of Hamburg under Albrecht Wezler (~2000–2004). He was an Associate Professor at Kyoto University (2006–2016) before joining the University of Oxford as a Fellow in 2016.
Dixian (1858–1932) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Mingzu (~1886–1889) and served as abbot of Guanzong Temple from around 1912 to 1932.

Dmitrij Nikolaevič Ovsjaniko-Kulikovskij (1853–1920) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Minaev, Jagić, and Bergaigne. He held professorships at Odesa University (1882–1887), Kazan State University (1887–1888), the University of Kharkiv (1888–1905), and Saint Petersburg State University (1905).

Dmitry Aleksandrovich Suleykin (1900–1948) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Fyodor Shcherbatskoy at Saint Petersburg State University (~1920–1924). He served as a naučnyj sotrudnik at the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts (1935–1938).

Dmitry Danilov works in philosophy and Indology. He studied at Mariupol State University, the University of Vienna, and Vasyl' Stus Donetsk National University, and was a PhD candidate at the H.S. Skovoroda Institute of Philosophy in 2015.

Dmitry Kudryavsky (1867–1920) was a linguist and Indologist who studied under Ivan Minaev in Saint Petersburg and Berthold Delbrück at Jena. He taught at Saint Petersburg (1895), University of Tartu (1898), and Voronezh State University (~1918–1920).
Do Trul Tubten Changchub Gyaltsen studied under Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö and Dodrupchen Rinpoche.
